models.label: wav2vec2-base phoneme CTC — INT8 (default)
models.notes: wav2vec2-base (94.4M params, bookbot/wav2vec2-ljspeech-gruut) fine-tuned for IPA phoneme CTC output. Dynamic INT8 quantization applied to MatMul/Gemm ops only — the 7-layer conv feature extractor and the positional conv embedding stayed FP32 because their weight-norm reparameterization (a Mul feeding Conv) isn't a quantizer-recognized constant initializer. FP32 source was 377.8MB; this build is 121.9MB (32%).

models.label: wav2vec2-base phoneme CTC — FP16 (diagnostic)
models.notes: Same checkpoint, weights/activations cast to FP16 (onnxconverter-common float16.convert_float_to_float16, keep_io_types=True so input_values/logits stay FP32 -- no harness changes needed). Added 2026-08-01 to test one hypothesis: real-iPad WebGPU steady-state latency on the INT8 build came back at ~572ms (mean, post-warmup, tight variance 540-631ms) -- over 3x the sandbox's own INT8-on-CPU number. INT8 kernels are far more mature on WASM/CPU than on current WebGPU backends across browsers, so INT8 may be actively hurting here rather than helping. FP16 rather than FP32 specifically because (a) FP16 is the precision GPUs -- including WebGPU -- are generally best optimized for, a more apt comparison than FP32, and (b) FP32 is 377.8MB, over wrangler's 300MiB `r2 object put` ceiling; FP16 halves that to 189.1MB. If FP16 is faster than INT8 on WebGPU, that confirms the quantization-is-hurting hypothesis; if FP16 is also 500ms+, the bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g. per-op GPU dispatch overhead across 12 transformer layers at this sequence length) and precision isn't the lever to pull. Verified correct (not just fast) against real speech from this repo's own voice pack before shipping, same as the INT8 build.
